title: Runtime Analysis and Asymptotics in C
subtitle: Trace it, count it, simplify it, and prove it.
description: A private, animation-supported C course that turns loop traces and recursive call chains into exact execution counts, limit comparisons, growth ordering, and formal O, Ω, and Θ proofs.
prerequisites: Comfort reading C loops, functions, arrays, and simple recursion.
Basic algebra, including powers, logarithms, and finite sums.
intendedFor: Learners who want to turn concrete C execution traces into exact runtime functions and rigorous asymptotic conclusions.
learningGoals: Trace loop variables and recursive arguments.
Build exact frequency-count runtime functions.
Classify function growth with the limit method.
Order common complexity classes.
Prove O, Ω, and Θ bounds with explicit constants and thresholds.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Complete the modules in order: exact counting, limit comparisons, inequality proofs, then the cumulative capstone.
courseOverview.summary: Use a repeatable tutor-style method: trace, count, sum, simplify, classify, and prove.

moduleSummary.title: Frequency Counting in C
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Make every iteration visible before introducing asymptotic notation.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Exact formulas for the Foo1 through Foo6 patterns and a justified dominant term.

moduleSummary.title: Asymptotics with Limits
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Move from exact formulas to formal asymptotic comparisons.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Correct O, Ω, and Θ classifications supported by limit calculations.

moduleSummary.title: Proofs from the Definitions
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Turn observed growth into definition-level proofs.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Formal Big-O, Big-Ω, and Big-Θ proofs with explicit constants.

moduleSummary.title: Runtime Analysis Capstone
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Combine the complete course method in one cumulative workspace.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: A complete analysis from source code to exact function and formal asymptotic bound.

authoringGuidance: This course must always use subjectSlug c, courseSlug c-runtime-analysis-asymptotics, and profileId c.
Teach with the sequence predict → trace → count → sum → simplify → classify.
Each topic begins with a tutor-style explanation and a manual step animation when state changes are central.
Do not replace exact counts with “two loops means n squared”; derive the actual frequency from the bounds.
Use symbolic reasoning as the proof and numerical C output only as a sanity check.
Use C11-compatible multi-file workspaces and deterministic fixed tests.

notes: Follow the teaching sequence: predict, trace values, count executions, form T(n), simplify, then classify.
Keep exact runtime analysis and asymptotic classification conceptually distinct even when they appear in the same topic.
Use manual animations for loop tables, triangular sums, moving bounds, recursive call chains, ratio limits, and proof thresholds.
Use C11-compatible code and deterministic fixed tests.

assessmentAndDelivery.suggestedBeginnerRhythm: One worked trace and one guided practice set per study session.
toolingSuggestions: C11 compiler through the shared Judge0 runner
Full IDE with explorer, editor, and output panel
assessmentAndDelivery.closingNote: Learners finish able to justify runtime bounds instead of guessing from surface syntax.

projectBrief.scenario: A teaching team needs a dependable runtime-analysis report for three unfamiliar C functions before adding them to an algorithms lesson. The report must show exact counts, tight growth classes, and a checked two-sided bound rather than guesses based only on the number of loops.
projectBrief.role: Junior C algorithm analyst preparing a reviewable complexity handoff
projectBrief.workspace: Browser multi-file C workspace with main.c, capstone.c, capstone.h, proof.c, and proof.h as required by the cumulative steps
projectBrief.deliverable: One three-step cumulative runtime-analysis project that derives exact operation counts for three functions, records their tight Theta classifications, and verifies explicit constants for a quadratic Theta proof.
requirements: Keep every step runnable as a complete C11 workspace.
Use tracing and frequency counting to derive exact formulas before stating asymptotic classes.
Preserve each earlier result when moving to the next cumulative step.
Classify each exact formula with a justified tight Theta bound.
Verify the final two-sided inequality with explicit c1, c2, and n0 values.
Use program output only as a deterministic check; the mathematical derivation remains the justification.

stepLadder.title: Derive the Exact Counts
stepLadder.requirement: Complete the counting functions so the workspace reports the exact Bar1, Bar2, and Bar3 operation totals for the authored input.

stepLadder.title: Classify the Dominant Terms
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve the exact-count work and record the tight Theta class for each of the three runtime functions.

stepLadder.title: Verify the Theta Proof
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve the earlier analysis and verify that 6n^2 <= T(n) <= 11n^2 for every n >= 1 using the authored proof workspace.
